info.title: Archiware P5 REST API
info.description:
The P5 REST API is a means of programmatically accessing the P5 software suite resources in order to integrate the P5 application server with third party solutions.

The REST API allows you to create, query, modify and destroy various P5 resources. A resource is, for example, client, filter, backup plan, archive plan, and the like. Resources are tracked in the P5 configuration database.
***
## P5 REST API Command Summary
All commands are defined by a http verb (GET, PUT, POST, DELETE) and by the resource URI requested. Different combinations invoke different P5 commands and return different results.

### Request URI
REST API commands are defined by their request URI, consisting of P5 server FQDN (including protocol) and resource path (e.g. https://localhost:8000/rest/archive/entries/). 

### Http verb meanings
Whenever possible, http verbs were kept consistent across commands:
                                          
GET   /rest/v1/resource_type/      --> returns a list of all resources of the given type                          

GET   /rest/v1/resource_type/ID    --> creates a new resource, returns ID and location links, request body may contain JSON formatted (complete) definition of the resourcereturns detailed information about the single resource instance

POST /rest/v1/resource_type/     --> creates a new resource, returns ID and location links, request body may contain JSON formatted (complete) definition of the resource                                                              

PUT   /rest/v1/resource_type/ID --> updates the existing resource, request body contains JSON formatted partial definition of the resource                                                                                        

DELETE   /rest/v1/resource_type/ID   --> deletes the existing resource; note that many resources do not support deletion but are stopped/canceled instead (e.g. running jobs)                                                   

POST    /rest/v1/resource_type/ID   --> executes some action on the resource (e.g. submit the backup job)           

However, some resources require special handling and have the general verb meaning slightly redefined. Please consult the command description in the following sections.

### Input parameters
Some commands require additional parameters to be passed with the request. For simple parameters, this is usually done by including the required parameter within the http request headers, as noted in the command description.\

For commands that accept more data (such as the description of the new resource or a list of path names), JSON formatted data must be included in the request body. Exact formatting is given with command description. Note that update commands (PUT) do not require all parameters given in the command description. Update operations will accept any subset of the listed parameters and will ignore any additional parameters not listed in the description.

200  --> OK                      -->  Operation completed successfully                                                                                      
202  --> Accepted                --> Operation accepted but not yet completed (corresponding job ID usually given in the response body)                   

207  --> Multi-status (Partial OK) -->  Operation partially successful, errors usually given in the response body                                               
400  --> Bar request              --> Invalid request (invalid JSON body, missing required header property, etc.)                                             
404  --> Not found                 --> Resource not found (invalid resource ID)                                                                             
409  --> Conflict                  --> Operation could not complete because of the conflicting resource state (e.g. stopping a job that is not currently running) 

500  --> Server error              --> Valid request but server encountered an error. Description either as a text or within JSON body.    

Note that not all commands return a response body. If there is no additional information necessary (apart from the command execution status code), no response body is given. When response contains new information, it is given either as a JSON formatted object or as a simple text string.

***

get.description:
Returns the list of Jobs tracked by the P5 server. Since information about each of the submitted jobs is held indefinitely, request by default returns only currently scheduled or running jobs. Response can be additionally customized by providing request header parameters.

Headers may include optional “filter = all | completed | failed | pending | running | warning” parameter, limiting the results to the provided job category. Additional parameter “lastdays=number” can be used to further limit the results to the indicated number of days (default is 0, showing only jobs for the current day).

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Either all, completed, failed, pending, running or warning

parameters.name: lastdays
parameters.description: Limit the results to this number of days. Default is 0 - show only the current day.

get.description:
Returns a completion protocol of the completed job in one of the three formats:

default human readable text:   
When no format is specified, the result is a human readable text. In this special case, the protocol may optionally also include one of the archived and/or restored files given by the optional “archiveentry” header value.

xml:
Providing the optional header property “format=xml” will change the output to the XML format. In this case, additional optional header property “filename=path” may be given in order to reroute the response to a file.

json:
Providing the optional header property "format=json" will change the output to the JSON object.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Output format

parameters.name: archiveentry
parameters.description: Archive entry resource

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: If set, the output will be redirected to this file. Only available if format is set to xml

get.description: Returns a report of the currently running job as a human readable text

Outputs a list of the files saved by the Job into a file. Headers must contain “filename=?client:? path” property, where “client” is the name of the P5 Client where to store the file and “path” is the complete path to the file to hold the output.

Headers may also include “attributes=list_of_attributes” property, indicating file system attributes and/or user defined metadata fields to be output in a tab separated format for each file. The supported system attributes are:       
  - “ppath” - the physical path of the file on the filesystem
  - “volumes” - a blank separated list of the volumes where the file is saved
  - “size” - the size of the saved file
  - “handle” - the handle, as required by the Restore selection
  - “btime” - the backup time of the file 
  - “mtime” - the file's modification time
  - “ino” - the inode number of the file

The index path returned by the inventory command cannot be used to access files on the file system in general. There are special cases where this might be used for this purpose, but generally it is not supported. The idea behind this info is to have an overview or idea what is being stored in the index and not to consume it in some other fashion (i.e. address the files on the file system to post-process them).

In cases where files are still expected to be in the file system at the place they were at the point of archiving (for example somebody wants to delete them or otherwise post-process them) the ppath attribute may be used, which, when given on the command line, will yield the physical path as- found on the client where the file resides. Note that not all index entries have corresponding physical paths. In such cases the value will be set to the string "<empty\>".

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Output file path, formatted as "?client:?path"

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description:
File system attributes and/or user defined metadata fields to be output in a tab separated format for each file.
Supports: ppath, volumes, size, handle, btime, mtime and ino

get.description: Get a list of all jukeboxes
Get detailed information about a jukebox

post.description:
Starts either an Inventory or Label job for the Jukebox. The headers must contain "action = inventory" or "action = label" key.

Inventory job effectively updates the internal volume database and returns the Job ID.
For Inventory, headers must contain parameters “startSlot=number” and “endSlot=number” (limiting the inventory job to a subset of configured Jukebox slots), and may contain additional argument: “barcode” with value “-barcode” (attempts a bar code inventory, instead of a default mount inventory).

Labels job labels media in the given jukebox for the given Pool, starting with slotID1, optionally including additional listed Slots.
Request body must contain JSON object specifying the Pool and Slots to be used.
Note that only new/empty volumes can be labeled with this command.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Either 'inventory' or 'label'

parameters.name: barcode
parameters.description: If set, attempts a bar code inventory. Only used if 'action = inventory'.

parameters.name: startSlot
parameters.description: Slot ID from which to start performing Inventory update. Only used if 'action = inventory'.

parameters.name: endSlot
parameters.description: The last Slot ID to be included in the Inventory update. Only used if 'action = inventory'.

delete.description: Performs a hardware jukebox reset, with forcefully emptying all jukebox drives. Use this method with caution since this command will perform an unconditional jukebox reset regardless of any jobs that may be using the jukebox resources.

get.description:
Returns the list of all volumes currently loaded in the Jukebox.

Note that slot IDs are numbered starting from 1, the id may differ from the numbering scheme of the library’s web interface.

In case a volume is present but unknown, a 0 is returned for that volume.
To update the list of the volumes in the jukebox, call POST rest/v1/jukeboxes/{jukeboxID}

parameters.name: slotID
parameters.description: If the slotID is given, returns only the volume in this slot.

Creates a new Media Pool resource.

Headers must include “name=string” property, indicating a name for the new resource. The name of the pool may not include blanks or any special punctuation characters. If the pool name already exists in the P5 configuration, an error will be thrown. 

The body may optionally contain json body specifying the additional pool parameters.

Get a list of all volumes
Get detailed information about a volume

post.description:
Outputs a list of the files contained on the Volume into a file. Headers must contain “filename=? client:?absolute_path” argument, whereby client is the name of the P5 client where to store the file and absolute_path is the complete path to the file to hold the output. The client part is optional and defaults to 'localhost:'.

The inventory command fills in the passed file with lines containing records separated by a TAB. If no <options> are given, the output file will by default contain the index paths of all the files saved by the given job <name>, one record per line. Additional <options> represent the attributes that will be output for each file in a tab-separated format. These attributes may be system attributes or any user-defined meta-data fields.

Note: This command can only be applied to Archive tapes

The supported system attributes are:
  - ppath -> the physical path of the file on the filesystem
  - size ->  the size of the saved file
  - handle -> the handle as required by the RestoreSelection
  - btime -> the backup time of the file
  - mtime -> the file's modification time
  - ino -> the inode number of the file
    
The index path returned by the inventory command cannot be used to access files on the file system in general. There are special cases where this might be used for this purpose, but generally it is not supported. The idea behind this info is to have an overview or idea what is being stored in the index and not to consume it in some other fashion (i.e. address the files on the file system to post-process them).

In cases where files are still expected to be in the file system at the place they were at the point of archiving (for example somebody wants to delete them or otherwise post-process them) the ppath attribute may be used, which, when given on the command line, will yield the physical path as-found on the client where the file resides. Note that not all index entries have corresponding physical paths. In such cases the value will be set to the string "<empty\>".

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: output file name, formatted as '?client:?absolute_path

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description: File system attributes and/or user defined metadata fields to be output in a tab separated format for each file. The supported system attributes are: “ppath” (physical path on the filesystem), “size”, “handle” (handle, as required by the Restore selection), “btime”, “mtime”, “ino” (inode number).

post.description: Submits the workstation backup job for execution to the server. Optional “time=now” (same as “time=0”) may be given to override plan execution time. Returns the job resource.

parameters.description: If set to 'now' or '0', the job will be sent to execution immedately, overriding the plan execution times.

delete.description: Deletes server resource, automatically stopping any scheduled job. If any jobs are running, the resource will not be deleted.

get.description: Get an overview of the current Archive state
Get a list of all plans

post.description: Create new plan

get.description: Get detailed information about a plan

post.description:
Submits one of the Archive plan operations (submit, run, verify) for execution and returns the corresponding Job ID. Headers must include “action” property.

“Submit” action submits the plan for execution. In order to run an Archive plan, an archive event must be selected. This  method thus selects the next planned archive event to start the archive plan. Optional “time=now” (or “time=0”) will override this scheduled execution time.

"Run” action runs the archive plan immediately with an optional delete pass on the target directory/ies.

"Verify" action re-runs the verify, clip generation and deletion (the post-archive tasks) of files located on the [client] computer and archived with the [jobId]. These parameters must be included in the request headers.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The action to execute on the Archive plan. Possible values are 'submit', 'run' or 'verify'.

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: If the action is 'submit', 'time=now' will override the scheduled execution time.

parameters.name: delete
parameters.description: If set, an additional delete pass on the target directories will be triggered. Usable only with 'action=run'.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Client ID to use for verification. Usable only with 'action=verify'.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: Job ID to use for verification. Usable only with 'action=verify'.

delete.description:
Stops the execution of the archive plan if it is currently running.
If the plan is sheduled but not currently running, it removes the plan from the scheduler.

409.description: Conflicting resource state (e.g. plan is neither running nor scheduled)

post.description:
Creates a new temporary Archive selection resource and immediately starts the Archive job

The new archive selection must be populated with files/folders, each of which can optionally be associated with metadata key/value pairs. Paths to be added as well as their metadata can be provided in the request body or the appropriate external input and output files must be referenced in headers.
Note that metadata keys must already be known in the index referenced by the Archive selection. Please use P5 GUI to add new metadata keys.

Paths ending with '*' will be added recursively. Folders should end with '/' or else they will be treated as files (only the directory node will be added, which is probably not the intended result).

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Client ID, as returned by 'GET /rest/v1/clients' request.

parameters.name: indexroot
parameters.description: Optional path. If set, all files in the archive selection will be indexed under this path.

parameters.name: inputfile
parameters.description:
Optional. However, if this is set, the outputfile must also be set.
If these keys are defined, request body will be ignored and the archive selection will be populated by parsing the inputfile.

File must be formatted with one entry per line, each entry in the format:
path [TAB] key1 [TAB] value1 [TAB] key2 [TAB] value2...
The path must be resolvable on the client for which the selection is created and the inputfile needs to reside on that client.

parameters.name: outputfile
parameters.description:
Optional. However, if this is set, the inputfile must also be set.
The output file will contain all accepted files with their ArchiveEntry handles used to reference the files later. The file format is one file per line in the format of:
path [TAB] handle

NOTE that when using external input/output files, folders are added as empty nodes. This means:
• folders are added without content, metadata in that case is assigned only to the folder
• If files are added into a non existing folder in the archive, the folder is created without attributes or metadata

parameters.name: addabsolute
parameters.description: If set, paths are added to index as-is. Any prefixes and alternative index destinations are ignored.

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: If set to 'now' or '0', overrides the scheduled execution time and starts now.

get.description: Gets the information about an Archive entry. The entry is calculated from the 'client' and 'path' keys given in headers. Optional 'database' key will limit the search to the corresponding database.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: The name of the P5 client where the <path> resides.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description:
The <path> is the absolute platform-native path to a file.
No checking is performed on the file. If the <path> contains { and/or } chars you must escape them with a backslash \ character.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: The optional <database> declares the name of the database where the file has been indexed. If omitted, the standard Default-Archive database is used.

get.description: Get detailed information about a entry

put.description: Update the Archive entry resource by changing the clippath and/or metadata. Does not support creating new metadata keys but only changing the values of the existing ones.

delete.description: Deletes Archive Entry specified by EntryId from Archive Index.

get.description: Get a list of all indexes

post.description: Creates the archive index database. If an archive index with the same [name] already exists, an error is thrown. The [name] must not contain blanks, special punctuation characters nor any special national characters. The [description] may contain any text.

get.description: Writes a backup copy of the archive index into the file indicated by the 'filename' key in headers

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Output file path.

put.description:
Outputs the Archive index Inventory to a file. Headers must include “filename=?client:? absolute_path” and optionally a list of attributes.

The inventory command fills in the passed file with lines containing records separated by a TAB. If no [attributes] are given, the output file will by default contain the index paths of all the files saved by the given job, one record per line. Additional [attributes] represent the attributes that will be output for each file in a tab-separated format. These attributes may be system attributes or any user-defined meta-data fields.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Output file name formatted as "?client:?absolute_path”, whereby client is the name of the P5 client where to store the file and absolute_path is the complete path to the file to hold the output. The client part is optional and defaults to 'localhost:'.

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description:
List of file system attributes to be incuded in the output in a tab separated format for each file.
 The supported attributes are: “ppath” (physical path on the filesystem), “volumes” (blank separated list of volumes where file is saved), “size”, “handle” (handle, as required by Restore selection), “btime”, “mtime”, “ino” (inode number)

post.description: Restores the Archive index database from the backup file indicated by the 'filename' property in the request headers.

get.description: Returns a list of snapshots contained in the Archive Index. Snapshots are timepoints (in Unix epoch format) for archive jobs that added content to the Archive.

Searches the Archive Index and lists its inventory content in a way similar to the Linux “ls“ command - showing content of a single tree level. The default URL can be followed by one or more path segments in order to list a different subpath.

Example: “GET /archive/indexes/Default-Archive/inventory/media/images/“ will list the content starting with the “/media/images/“ directory. Each element will conatain a link to itself, simplifying drilling down through directory structure.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: Archive snapshot (as returned by GET /archive/indexes/{ID}/snapshots). Filters the results to only include files saved during this particular Archive job.

get.description: Get a list of all keys

put.description:
Updates the existing Archive index keys and their meta attributes. Supports creation of new keys bud does not delete existing keys not defined in the request body.

Keyname must not contain blank or exceed 15 characters. Type must be one of 'C' (character key) or 'N' (numeric key). 

Note that type property for the existing keys cannot be changed. Attributes and values for metadata must also not exceed 15 characters each.

post.description:
Updates the Archive index keys and their meta attributes (supports creation of new keys). Key schema given in the request body is considered final – keys are added and deleted accordingly.

Keyname must not contain blanks or exceed 15 characters. Type must be one of 'C' (character key) or 'N' (numeric key). Attributes and values for metadata must also not exceed 15 characters each.

get.description: Get detailed information about a key

delete.description: Deletes the user defined key from the archive index.

Create a new synchronize plan.
  
Expects a json object in body with at least the 'description' attribute set. If any other attributes are set, the plan will be automatically updated with the given values.

get.description: Get detailed information about a plan

post.description:
Executes the Synchronize plan Start or Run operation, depending on the “action” property specified in the headers. Returns the corresponding Job ID. Headers must include “action=run” or “action=submit”. 

'Submit' action submits the plan for execution. The headers may include optional “time=now” (or “time=0”) which will override scheduled execution time. Plan must be configured for auto-start since API just overrides the scheduled starting time. This command cannot be used to start a plan which is not set to auto-start or which does not have any events configured.

 'Run' action runs the plan immediately. The headers may include optional “delete=true” which will trigger the additional delete pass on the target directory. Note: In order to run a Synchronize plan, a Synchronize event must be selected. This method implicitly selects the next planned event to start the plan.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Either 'run' or 'submit'.

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: If set to 'now' or '0', overrides the scheduled execution time and starts now. Only usable with action=submit

parameters.name: delete
parameters.description: If set, triggers the additional delete pass on the target directory. Only usable with action=run

delete.description: Cancels the execution (if running) or removes the scheduled Synchronize plan from execution schedule

409.description: Conflicting resource state (e.g. plan is neither running nor scheduled)

 'Run' action runs the plan immediately. Note: In order to run a Object Synchronize plan, a Object Synchronize event must be selected. This method implicitly selects the next planned event to start the plan.

post.description:
Creates new temporary Restore selection resource and runs the corresponding restore job.

Headers must contain “client=ID” property. Optionally, headers may contain “relocate=path” property, overriding the default restore location. If this option is given, it must point to a directory on the client file system (will be created if needed).

Restore selection can be populated in several ways:

** Restore entries may be given as “entries”, in which case they must include Archive entry ID (as returned by the “POST /rest/v1/archive/plans/{ID}/archiveselections” request).
Optional “targetPath” property will specify the target path of the restored file.

NOTE: The “relocate“ property applies to all restore selection entries and is prepended to the restore path. The “targetPath“ property applies to the single entry for which it was defined and completely defines the rest of the final path, in addition to the “relocate“ part, if given.

Example: Given the original path = “/my/old/path/file1“, relocate = “/restored“ and targetPath = “/some/folder/recovered_01“, the actual path to the restored file will be “/restored/some/folder/recovered_01“. 

** Restore entries may also be defined as “searches”, allowing P5 to automatically find and add the correct Archive entry handle. In this case, “archivePlan” property contains the Archive Plan ID and “expression” contains the search expression used to locate the records. The expression has the following generic format:

[key1] [op1] [val1] && [key2] [op2] [val2] ...

The [key] is the name of the key as passed during archiving of the entry (“POST /rest/v1/archive/plans/{ID}/archiveselections” or “PUT /rest/v1/archive/plans/{ID}/archiveselections/{ID}”) The [op] is the logical operation applied to the value. The [val] is the value associated with the key. The following logical operations are supported: "==" key equals the value "*=" key starts with value 

Example:

{author *= marco && state == italy}

When searching for files or folders by filename, the key/value “name” must be used. Example: {name == myfile.pdf} or {name *= 'my file'}
When entering expressions, please put curly braces around the complete expression. Values in expressions can be enclosed in single quotes, in case the value contains one or more blanks, it must be enclosed in single quotes.

NOTE: Only entries that are located on "known" or "accessible" volumes are reported. If an entry is found in the index but is located on "inaccessible" volume (volume is disabled, not currently mounted in some tape drive or not found in any known media changer), it is not included in the selection.

** Restore selection can be added from external file or from a specified volume

status.description:
The status of the archived entry.
An archive entry can have number of internal statuses, depending on the stage of the archive and/or restore process. Currently, the following statuses are supported:
  • indexed - found in the archive index
  • unknown - not found in the archive index
The indexed status means that the entry has been processed (archived) and its meta data may be obtained from the index database.
The unknown status means that the entry has not (yet) been found in the index, which is normal for files still waiting to be archived.

onjobactivation.description:
Registers the [command] to be executed just before the job is started by the submit method. The command itself can be any valid OS command plus variable number of arguments.
The very first argument of the command (the program itself) can be prepended with the name of the P5 client where the command is to be executed on.
If omitted, the command will be executed on the client which the ArchiveSelection object is created for.

Examples:
"mickey:/var/scripts/myscript arg"
will execute /var/scripts/myscript on the client "mickey" regardless of the client the ArchiveSelection is created for. The program will be passed one argument: arg.

"/var/scripts/myscript"
will execute /var/scripts/myscript on the client the ArchiveSelection is created for.

"localhost:/var/scripts/myscript"
will execute /var/scripts/myscript on the P5 server.

onjobcompletion.description: Registers the [command] to be executed immediately after the job created by the submit method is completed. See onjobactivation for further

onfiledeletion.description: Registers the [command] to be executed immediately after the files are deleted through a job created by the submit method. See onjobactivation for further information.

Recurrence type: "D" daily, "W" weekly or "M" monthly

W: \<count\> \<days\> (list of numbers 1-7 for Mon-Sun)

M: \<count\> \<week\> (1-5) \<day\> (1-7, single value)

Examples: "D 7" - every 7 days

"W 2 1 2 3 4 5" - every 2 weeks on Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu and Fri

"M 1 5 6" - every month on the last week (5) Saturday (6)

label.description:
Returns the (human readable) job label.
The following labels are returned: Archive, Backup, Synchronize and System.

description.description: A (human readable) job description as shown in the P5 job monitor

status.description:
Returns the status of the job. A job can have a number of internal statuses, depending on the stage of the archive and/or restore process. Currently, the following statuses are supported:
  • started -  the job is starting (intermediate state)
  • stopped  -  the job is stopping (intermediate state)
  • unknown - the job is not known by the system
  • scheduled - the job is in the queue waiting to be run
  • pending - an intermediate state during start, the job is waiting to be accepted for start by the queue manager
  • running - the job is running
  • canceled - the job is canceled by user
  • completed - the job is completed
  • terminated - the job is terminated by a server shutdown

completion.description:
The completion code of the completed job. The completion code can be one of
    • success
    • exception
    • failure
    
The success completion code means that the job has completed successfully in its entirety. It does not mean that all of the files have been archived and/or restored, though. For info about the particular file, use the protocol method.

The exception completion code means that parts of the job have failed, but the job may have been partially executed successfully. This happens for parallel archive/restore operations where one of the job threads runs into an error, while others continue to run and finish successfully.
The failure completion code means that the job has failed in its entirety and none of the files have been processed (archived/restored) correctly.

linkcycles.description:
Enable/disable using file system snapshots and links as a cycle creation method.

  If enabled, file system snapshots are used  when available (ZFS, BtrFS). Where not supported, files are created by hard links.
  If disabled, all files are copied to the cycle and each cycle requires the entire original capacity.

Get/set the criteria for comparing source and target files.  Expects a list of available options:


  mtime – file modification time
  
  ctime – file access and/or attribute changes
  
  size – file size changes

twopass.description:
Enable/disable using deletion mode in two passes.

  When enabled, P5 recursively compares source and target directories in two passes. The first pass deletes all files and folders from the target that have been remved from the source. The second pass copies new and changed files. Benefit: deletes stale data from the target up-front, freeing up space for new data.

  When disabled, both steps are performed in a single pass. Benefit: faster operation.

loglevel.description:
Get/set log level verbosity. Possible values are:
  
  0 – log errors only
  
  1 – log errors and file operations

numworkers.description:
Get/set the number of parallel file transfers.

  When set to 1, files are transferred sequentially from source to destination. Benefit: less system load.
  
  When set to a higher value, multiple files are simultaneously transferred from the source to the destination. Benefit: Significant increase in throughput when very fast disk subsystems such as Solid State Drives (SSD) are used.

cycleworkers.description: Get/set the number of threads generating a new sync cycle for filesystems that are not snapshot-capable. For filesystems located on SSD devices this may reduce cycle building time when handling lots of files and directories. Recommended value depends on your installation but it is usually something between 2 and 4.

transfermode.description: Enable/disable transfer mode. If enabled, Sync will delete data from the source folder after successfully copying it over to the destination.

verification.description:
File veryfication checksum algorithm. Possible values are:
  {}, crc32, md5, sha224, sha256, sha384, sha512, xxh3_64, xxh3_128

maxversions.description: The number of file versions to keep when Incremental-Synchronize takes place.

maxcycles.description: The number of cycles to keep. A cycle begins with a full synchronization, is terminated with the next full synchronization and contains all the changes that were incrementally synced in-between.

linkcycles.description:
Enable/disable using file system snapshots and links as a cycle creation method.

  If enabled, file system snapshots are used  when available (ZFS, BtrFS). Where not supported, files are created by hard links.
  If disabled, all files are copied to the cycle and each cycle requires the entire original capacity.

preprocessor.description: The script to be executed before synchronize

postprocessor.description: The script to be executed after synchronize

runpostonerr.description: Enable/disable running the postprocessor script always, even on job errors or exceptions.

filecheck.description:
Get/set the criteria for comparing source and target files.  Expects a list of available options:


  mtime – file modification time
  
  ctime – file access and/or attribute changes
  
  size – file size changes

twopass.description:
Enable/disable using deletion mode in two passes.

  When enabled, P5 recursively compares source and target directories in two passes. The first pass deletes all files and folders from the target that have been remved from the source. The second pass copies new and changed files. Benefit: deletes stale data from the target up-front, freeing up space for new data.

  When disabled, both steps are performed in a single pass. Benefit: faster operation.

loglevel.description:
Get/set log level verbosity. Possible values are:
  
  0 – log errors only
  
  1 – log errors and file operations

numworkers.description:
Get/set the number of parallel file transfers.

  When set to 1, files are transferred sequentially from source to destination. Benefit: less system load.
  
  When set to a higher value, multiple files are simultaneously transferred from the source to the destination. Benefit: Significant increase in throughput when very fast disk subsystems such as Solid State Drives (SSD) are used.

cycleworkers.description: Get/set the number of threads generating a new sync cycle for filesystems that are not snapshot-capable. For filesystems located on SSD devices this may reduce cycle building time when handling lots of files and directories. Recommended value depends on your installation but it is usually something between 2 and 4.

paths.description:
The list of directory paths to be added to the Sync selection. Each itmes is an absolute path to the directory to be synced. The directories must be located on the source client and under the source path as given in the sync plan used to create the sync selection object. Paths containing spaces must be delimitied with { and } braces.
Paths ending in '*' will be added recursively.

onjobactivation.description:
Registers the command to be executed just before the job is started. The command itself can be any valid OS command plus variable number of arguments.
The very first argument of the command (the program itself) can be prepended with the name of the P5 client where the command is to be executed on. If omitted, the command will be executed on the client which the SyncSelecttion object is created for.

Examples:
"mickey:/var/myscript arg"
will execute /var//myscript on the client "mickey" regardless what client the SyncSelection is created for. The program will be passed one argument: arg.

"/var/scripts/myscript"
will execute /var/scripts/myscript on the client the SyncSelection is created for.

"localhost:/var/scripts/myscript"
will execute /var/scripts/myscript on the P5 server.

onjobcompletion.description: Registers the command to be executed immediately after the job is completed. See 'onjobactivation' for more details.

start.description: Set/get the absolute time in seconds (Posix time) for the first run. All subsequent runs will be scheduled starting from this time and using the frequency and exception rules.

frequency.description:
Sync frequency given as a schedule encoding string in a (somewhat) human readable format as follows: 

  Recurrence type: "D" daily, "W" weekly or "M" monthly

  Time encoding: D: \<count\>

  W: \<count\> \<days\> (list of numbers 1-7 for Mon-Sun)

  M: \<count\> \<week\> (1-5) \<day\> (1-7, single value)

  Examples: "D 7" - every 7 days

  "W 2 1 2 3 4 5" - every 2 weeks on Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu and Fri

  "M 1 5 6" - every month on the last week (5) Saturday (6)

exception.description: Exceptions to the Sync frequency given in the same format as above.

filter.description: File filter ID as returned by 'GET /rest/v1/general/filters'

mode.description:
The Sync mode for this event. Supported modes are:
  
  mirror - Keep target identical to source, perform deletes where necessary.
  
  update - Copy only modified and new files. Do not delete on target.

cycles.description: Enable/disable keeping previous data as a cycle. Applicable only if mode is set to mirror.

versions.description: Enable/disable keeping previous file versions. Applicable only if mode is set to update.

events.description:
Enable/disable using file system events to detect new or changed files. 

  If enabled, the Operating System notifies P5 about all changes in a files system. Based on this the synchronize process can very quickly locate new or changed files. Disadvantage: In some circumstances single fs-events can be lost, e.g. when the server reboots or on a heavily loaded system.
  
  If disabled, P5 scans the file system. This is the most reliable way to find new or changed files. Disadvantage: Scanning a large file system can be a time-consuming  process.
